evidence.note: Read golden NOA/EDA/BIF files carefully before implementing to reverse-engineer exact output format; goldens drove the implementation, but this is pre-implementation format-reading, not diffing to localize failures.

Ran a targeted single-component test (sif_triangle_noa) repeatedly — a level-5-style focused invocation — but the loop was consumed by compilation/path fixes; once it passed the agent moved on without any byte-diff step.

After full-suite runs the agent only read pass/fail counts ('25 pass, 234 fail') and attributed failures to unimplemented stubs; it never inspected actual-vs-golden byte differences to diagnose any failing test.
Debugging was entirely compilation-error and count-driven (mass regex/Python patching); no hex/whitespace inspection, minimal-input probes, or intermediate-output comparisons ever appear.

reasoning: The agent leveraged golden files to specify the target format and did run targeted single-test invocations, which lifts it slightly above the pure anchor-3 'reads pass/fail counts' behavior. However, it never once inspected actual-vs-golden byte differences to diagnose a failing test, and constructed no auxiliary checks (hex, whitespace, minimal inputs, intermediate outputs) — the defining behaviors of anchors 5 and 8. Its failure diagnosis was count-based and stub-attribution-based, placing it at a 4, interpolating between anchors 3 and 5.
